story_facts: P000719. King wears uniform of colonel of the Guardia de Corps with royal orders incl. Order of Carlos III; painted as pendant to the Queen's equestrian portrait (same room); registered at Madrid Royal Palace 1814, entered Prado 1819.

P000720. Pendant to Carlos IV on Horseback; she rides 'Marcial', a horse given by Godoy, with El Escorial and the Guadarrama behind; Goya drew on Velázquez's equestrian Isabel de Borbón (which he had etched in 1778); letters between Queen and Godoy describe sittings Sept-Oct 1799.

P007767. NOTE: page shows 'Room C' (letter, not a numbered gallery) - verify on site. Sitter María Teresa de Borbón y Vallabriga, raised in a Toledo convent, married Godoy 1797; wheat ears in her hair evoke Ceres/fertility (she was expecting); X-rays show Goya reused a canvas with a standing Godoy and beneath that a young knight of the Order of Malta.

P000723. Goya shows himself vulnerable and calm; fast crossing 'Venetian' brushstrokes in the background vs finer detail on face; looks straight at the viewer (not into a mirror) and scratched his signature/date into the wet paint, possibly with the brush handle. (Same room also has tiny 1795 Self-Portrait P007775, 18x12 cm.)
P002899. Painted near the end of his life in Bordeaux; light palette contrasts with the Black Paintings; low viewpoint makes her seem to ride a mule; milk jug behind her at left.

P000780. Expected 093 CONFIRMED. Tapestry cartoon (original, 259x220) from series Mengs commissioned in Oct 1777 for the Asturias princes' bedroom at El Pardo; Goya's invoice describes Valencian crockery seller, two young ladies, old woman, lady in coach; read as vanitas / unfulfilled desire (lady in coach gazing wistfully).

official_title: The Painter's Children in the Japanese Room
story_facts: P002931. Expected 063B CONFIRMED. His son Mariano (~3) and daughter María Luisa in the Japanese Room of Villa Arata, Portici; meant as a gift for his father-in-law Federico de Madrazo, left unfinished at Fortuny's sudden death; flat walls, butterflies, fan and wide format show Japanese influence.

official_title: Amalia de Llano y Dotres, Countess of Vilches
story_facts: P002878. Painted aged 32; she wrote novels (Berta, Ledia) and sang at Madrazo family soirées; Ingres-trained refinement - hand on fan, smile, gaze; Prado calls it the most emblematic 19th-c. work in its collection.

P000864. Expected 062A CONFIRMED. Painted when 80-year-old Goya briefly returned from Bordeaux exile to settle his pension; his most famous likeness, more than his self-portraits; legend says Goya told López to leave it unfinished; inscription 'Lopez a su amigo Goya'.

P002200 (the 1767 prime version; a 1774 version P5011 is a copy). Became the king's official image - Grimaldi had replicas sent to foreign courts incl. one requested by the Empress of Russia; armour, Golden Fleece, Holy Ghost order, baton; pendant to Queen Maria Amalia painted posthumously from other likenesses.

P002197. Painted soon after he arrived in Spain: velvet gown, tools of his trade; loose sketchy technique lets the priming show through; Mengs also appears in his Adoration of the Shepherds (P2204). (Other 'Portrait of Mengs' pages are Carmona prints / Fabregat drawing - NOT on display.)

official_title: Queen Christina of Sweden, on Horseback
story_facts: P001503. Artwork page location = 'Ábside' (no number); 2026 exhibition page 'Christina of Sweden. A passion for sculpture' places it in the Hall of the Muses - consistent with notes. Rearing horse = power; falconer/dogs = royal hunting; sent to Philip IV (she gave it herself) to affirm her Catholic alignment; hung in the Alcázar by 1666; near-identical copy in Stockholm Nationalmuseum.

P002402. Opens the Room 74 display (exhibition 10 Jun 2026 - 2 Jul 2027). Bourdon was her court painter from 1652; sceptre, plain black silk with a man's-style ribbon reflecting her masculine dress; only jewel a cameo ring - nod to her love of antiquity.

E000167. Ariadne asleep on Naxos after Theseus abandoned her, Dionysus about to arrive; Roman copy of a Pergamene model c.150 BC, restored in Bernini's workshop; once called 'Cleopatra' (incl. in Christina's collection).

E000029. Found 1675 near the Chiesa Nuova in an ancient sculptor's workshop (hence unfinished surface); restored by Ferrata; twisting pose seen as forerunner of Baroque; Christina -> Azzolino -> Odescalchi -> La Granja.

E000033. Crouching bather after Doidalsas of Bithynia; tortoise = domestic virtue (carries its house, thought tongueless = quiet wife, per Plutarch); 17th-c. restorers raised her arm with a perfume bottle; Cardinal Massimo -> Christina -> Spain.

E000022. Ovid's nymph turned into a heliotrope gazing at the sun; ancient lower part, torso/head/arm added by Cartari 1665-80; sun motif evokes Christina's personal emblem; later in Isabel de Farnesio's collection.

P000722. NOT the Black Painting 'La Leocadia'; long misidentified as Goya's wife Josefa Bayeu (she died 1812 aged 65, sitter is ~30s); dress details date it c.1812-14; sitter now tentatively Leocadia Zorrilla, Goya's companion.

P000735. Purple ermine robe, sceptre with arms of Castile-León, Order of Carlos III, Golden Fleece; X-ray changes suggest Goya painted the king from life; Ferdinand abolished the Constitution and ruled as absolute monarch.

P002898. Painted in Bordeaux May 1827 aged 81 - possibly his last known work; sitter a liberal banker exiled for his ideas; trembling loose strokes yet near-miniature face and hands. (Room 066 also = E40 Milkmaid.)

official_title: The 2nd of May 1808 in Madrid or "The Fight against the Mamelukes"
story_facts: P000748. NOTE Room 064 (not 065/066) - no Goya found confirmed in 065. Commissioned by the Regency 1814; Goya painted only two May 1808 scenes, not four; damaged in a 1938 truck accident at Benicarló, restored 2007-08.

official_title: The 3rd of May 1808 in Madrid or "The Executions"
story_facts: P000749. Room 064. Pendant to 2nd of May; faceless firing squad vs lit victims; lower-left damage from 1937 Civil War transfer to Valencia.

official_title: General José de Palafox on Horseback
story_facts: P000725. Room 064. Hero of the 1808 siege of Zaragoza; commissioned by the sitter; theatrical pose hints at vanity; bequeathed by his son.
P000724. Room 064. Probably commissioned by the School of Highway Engineers; engineers at work behind; no campaign explains the king in a camp - a puzzle.
P001036. Room 055 (Spanish court portraits). Pendant to her Anne of Austria; X-ray shows she replaced a bulky cape and moved his hand to the chair arm; golden rosary alludes to Lepanto.

official_title: Infantas Isabel Clara Eugenia and Catalina Micaela
story_facts: P001138. Philip II's daughters, painted repeatedly to plan marriages; later Duchess of Savoy and Governor of the Netherlands; wreath may borrow from Van Eyck's Arnolfini (then in Philip II's collection).

artist: Juan Pantoja de la Cruz (after Sofonisba Anguissola)
story_facts: P001030. Copy replacing Sofonisba's original lost in the 1604 El Pardo fire; gold marten's head hints at duty to bear an heir; Sofonisba was the queen's lady-in-waiting and painting teacher.
P002108. Painted on Charles V's orders when Mary married Prince Philip (11 years younger) in 1554; pose follows Raphael's Julius II; Mor softened plain features with majesty.
P007614. Father and six children; hourglass and skull = vanitas; absent mother suggests a family united in grief; bought 1992 (Villaescusa Legacy).

E000228. Only 058B item found. Bears Philip V's cross mark; marble possibly reused from antiquity; style named after Emperor Frederick II 'Stupor Mundi' whose love of antiquity sparked a proto-Renaissance.
P002678. Valencian taste for gold; Renaissance architecture with Flemish-style figures; angels guide Mary and Joseph; Pablo Bosch bequest 1916; original frame catalogued separately.
P000851. Raphael-influenced poses; Flemish-style landscape includes Baptism of Christ; round panel pair with Martyrdom of St Agnes from San Julián, Valencia.
P000842. From the San Esteban altarpiece, Valencia (with Juanes' Last Supper); composition echoes the Entombment of Christ; a man in contemporary dress looking out is probably a patron.
P002707. Mary seated on a cushion, not a throne - closer to worshippers (mendicant devotion); soft Valencian International Gothic; Pablo Bosch bequest 1916.

official_title: Virgen de la Leche with Saint Bernard and Saint Benedict
story_facts: P008446. Lactation miracle: milk from the Virgin's breast gives St Bernard eloquence; etched gold background; bought 2022 at Subastas Segre.

official_title: The Creation of Adam, Hermitage of Vera Cruz, Maderuelo (Segovia)
story_facts: P007285. Whole Romanesque chapel interior removed 1947 and rebuilt in the Prado; paired with Original Sin; flat outlined figures compared to the Master of Tahull.

official_title: Saint Dominic of Silos enthroned as a Bishop
story_facts: P001323. EXTRA (051A, adjacent). Centre of Daroca altarpiece; Flemish-style realism in vestments and gilded throne; virtues personified around him; Prado acquired 1920.
P002998. EXTRA (051A). No wounds or blood - drama from the embrace and tears; tiny donors pray 'Miserere mei Domine'; probably for a funerary monument.
P007710. EXTRA (051A). Scallop-shell pilgrim of Compostela; Juan de Flandes served Isabella the Catholic and lost his salary at her death.
P006895. EXTRA (051A). Left panel of Pietà altarpiece from Ejea de los Caballeros; armoured archangel spears a dragon-demon.
P002825. EXTRA (058, next to 058B). Made for the Leuven crossbowmen's guild (tiny crossbows in corners); skull marks Adam's grave; fainting Virgin mirrors dead Christ.

official_title: The Temptations of Saint Anthony Abbot
story_facts: P002913. EXTRA (056A, not 056). Dendro dates it to Bosch's lifetime; probably a close follower; focuses on Eve's sin (apple), brothel symbols.

P000211. One of five versions (Louvre, Dulwich, Ponce, Auckland); a 1619 letter mentions a patron awaiting 'the arrow-pierced Martyr'; Isabel Farnese owned it at La Granja 1746; cleaning removed repaints on the loincloth.
P000201. Painted for Cardinal Alessandro Ludovisi; Daniel 13 story; Susanna's pose from the Crouching Aphrodite; an elder reaches toward us, making viewers voyeurs.
P001635. Quack wears a necklace of pulled teeth as advertising; diplomas possibly fake; Caravaggesque crowd watching and waiting their turn.

official_title: The Beheading of Saint John the Baptist
story_facts: P000258. EXTRA (007A). Part of a Baptist series for the Buen Retiro also commissioned from Artemisia Gentileschi; moment before the blow; strong chiaroscuro.

P001112. Blind man feeling a sculpted head - the paragone debate (painting vs sculpture, which can be known by touch); once misidentified as blind sculptor Gonnelli; earlier version in Norton Simon, Pasadena.
P001099. From an apostle series (Counter-Reformation); holds the knife of his flaying; Alcázar inventory 1701-03 valued it at 50 doubloons.
P007077. Room 040 is the 'Sala de Copias' (copies room). A 20th-c. El Greco pastiche/fake - an old inventory labels it 'Greco (falso)'; X-ray shows a much later added figure.
P007782. Full-scale copy of the Borghese Titian made by a Rome pensionado as training; page says it is in the museum's 'Sala de Copias'; reached the Prado 2016.
P000438. Later version of a subject first painted for Philip II's chapel at El Escorial; Simon of Cyrene may portray mosaicist Francesco Zuccato; Christ's tearful gaze meets ours.
P000428. Strips away the servant and setting of his 1516 Doria Pamphilj version; Lavinia-as-model claim rejected; X-rays show her left arm and eyes were moved.
P000498. Painted after his 1573 Inquisition interrogation over Feast in the House of Levi - darker, simpler, more modest; tears = contrition (Chrysostom).
